# Tutorial topic guide {.unnumbered}

This guide describes the focus of each tutorial in the [weekly schedule](schedule.qmd). It complements the [lecture topic guide](topics.qmd) by emphasizing the concepts and methods that students will practise.

<!--

## Normal-form games {#sec-tutorial-normal-form-games}

The tutorial introduces the practical representation and analysis of finite
strategic games.

**Tutorial focus:** constructing and reading payoff matrices; identifying action
profiles and best responses; testing strict and weak dominance; iterated
elimination of dominated actions; finding pure-strategy Nash equilibria;
comparing equilibrium outcomes with Pareto-optimal outcomes.

## Nash equilibrium {#sec-tutorial-nash-equilibrium}

The tutorial develops the calculations needed to work with mixed strategies and
equilibrium conditions.

**Tutorial focus:** computing expected payoffs; deriving best-response and
indifference conditions; solving small games in mixed strategies; determining
supports; verifying whether a proposed strategy profile is a Nash equilibrium.

## Two-player zero-sum games {#sec-tutorial-zero-sum-games}

The tutorial uses the zero-sum structure to connect equilibrium analysis with
optimization.

**Tutorial focus:** locating pure saddle points; computing maximin and minimax
values; formulating the players' linear programs; interpreting primal and dual
solutions as equilibrium strategies; applying best-response and double-oracle
reasoning.

## Computing Nash equilibrium {#sec-tutorial-computing-nash-equilibrium}

The tutorial applies systematic methods for finding equilibria in finite
general-sum games.

**Tutorial focus:** selecting candidate supports; setting up indifference
equations; checking actions outside the proposed supports; support enumeration;
testing candidate equilibria through pure deviations and feasibility
conditions.

## Alternatives to Nash equilibrium {#sec-tutorial-alternatives}

The tutorial works with equilibrium concepts that incorporate correlation or
commitment.

**Tutorial focus:** writing correlated-equilibrium incentive constraints;
checking a proposed correlated distribution; formulating correlated-equilibrium
computation as a linear program; finding follower best responses; distinguishing
weak and strong Stackelberg equilibria under different tie-breaking rules.

## Selected exercises {#sec-tutorial-selected-exercises}

This tutorial consolidates the strategic-form material from the preceding
weeks. The teaching assistant will announce the exact selection and emphasis.

## Midterm test {#sec-tutorial-midterm-test}

The tutorial time is reserved for the midterm test. Its point value, structure,
and requirements are described in the
[assessment and grading information](assessment.qmd#midterm-test).

## Extensive-form games {#sec-tutorial-extensive-form-games}

The tutorial practises representing sequential interaction and reasoning at
every decision point in a game tree.

**Tutorial focus:** identifying histories, terminal nodes, player and chance
moves, and information sets; specifying complete contingent strategies;
constructing the induced normal form; applying backward induction; checking
subgame-perfect equilibrium and credible behavior.

## Solving extensive-form games {#sec-tutorial-solving-extensive-form-games}

The tutorial develops computational representations for games with imperfect
information.

**Tutorial focus:** listing sequences; constructing realization plans and their
flow constraints; setting up sequence-form linear programs for two-player
zero-sum games; interpreting best responses; understanding incremental strategy
generation and counterfactual-regret methods.

## Auctions {#sec-tutorial-auctions}

The tutorial applies Bayesian-game analysis to standard auction formats.

**Tutorial focus:** modelling types, valuations, bids, allocation, and payments;
computing winning probabilities and interim expected utility; deriving or
checking symmetric Bayes-Nash equilibrium bidding strategies; comparing
first-price and second-price auctions; using revenue equivalence under its
stated assumptions.

## Mechanism design {#sec-tutorial-mechanism-design}

The tutorial analyses allocation and payment rules through their incentive
properties.

**Tutorial focus:** distinguishing types from reports; checking dominant-strategy
incentive compatibility and individual rationality; working with monotone
allocation rules and their payment rules; applying virtual valuations;
computing outcomes and payments under the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves mechanism.

## Coalitional games {#sec-tutorial-coalitional-games}

The tutorial practises evaluating cooperation and the stability of proposed
allocations.

**Tutorial focus:** specifying a transferable-utility characteristic function;
computing coalition values and marginal contributions; writing efficiency and
coalitional-rationality constraints; checking whether an allocation belongs to
the core; analysing core emptiness in small games.

## Shapley value {#sec-tutorial-shapley-value}

The tutorial computes fair allocations from marginal contributions.

**Tutorial focus:** calculating marginal contributions for different player
orders; evaluating the Shapley formula in small games; checking efficiency,
symmetry, the null-player property, and additivity; interpreting the result as
an expected marginal contribution.
